ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each partner, director, general partner, ultimate beneficial owner and senior manager will be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN (Specially Designated Nationals) List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Macao Monetary Authority restrictive measures, and the Macao Financial Intelligence Office internal Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and their family members or close associates, requiring independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds for each maritime installment payment. Additional checks under ISIC 3011 include vessel end-user certification and denial orders from the PRC Ministry of Commerce and the U.S. Commerce Entity List. All screening results must be documented, maintained for at least ten years after termination of the business relationship, and made instantly available to the Macao Financial Intelligence Office upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Macao Commercial and Movable Property Registry (Registo Comercial e de Bens Móveis de Macau) electronic name search and reservation platform (ComServiços)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 14 to 19 of the Macao Commercial Code, a partnership name must contain a distinctive denomination token, a business object phrase, a legal form indicator, and a jurisdiction marker (four-tier naming convention). The name must be established in Portuguese, Chinese, or both; an English transliteration may be registered only as a secondary name. All Chinese characters must be standard simplified forms if mainland China cross-border filings are anticipated, and the Portuguese transliteration must be phonetically accurate and published in the Macao Official Gazette. Reserved names must not be identical or deceptively similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under the Macao Commercial Code, any name rejection notice issued by the Commercial and Movable Property Registry must be administratively appealed within ten working days. The applicant must submit a written petition to the Director of the Registry, attaching the original search receipt, the full rejection decision, correct legal basis citations, and three alternative naming structures. If the Registry upholds the refusal, the applicant may file a further appeal with the Macao Administrative Court within thirty days, invoking procedural breach, lack of statutory prohibition, or disproportionate restriction. The appeal also lodges a request for ancillary injunction preventing another applicant from reserving the contested name while judicial review is pending. Corrected naming alternatives should be included in every submission to expedite reconsideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 3011 commercial shipbuilding yard, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is categorically rejected by the Macao Tax Authority (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças), the Macao Economic and Technological Development Bureau, and the Municipal Affairs Bureau because the industrial and environmental operating license requires a physical factory address, evidence of marine fabrication capability, dry-dock layout, and employment of industrial safety and environmental officers. A serviced address may be used only for correspondence collection, but cannot satisfy the statutory registered office requirement for a shipyard. Banks financing maritime installment letters of credit will reject a virtual office and will demand on-site due diligence before opening the corporate account.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (a) physical dry-dock and slipway presence; (b) welding certificates and machinery safety inspection records; (c) wastewater and oil-spill environmental permits; (d) industrial accident and employer liability insurance; (e) full attendance and work-permit records for any non-resident workers; (f) crane load-testing and fire safety certificates. Quantified risk: extremely high; unannounced inspections by the Macao Labour Affairs Bureau, Tax Authority, Fire Services Bureau, and the Environment Protection Bureau occur in 80-100% of newly licensed shipyards within the first twelve months, and at least one statutory inspection every six months is mandatory for industrial employers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Macao Special Administrative Region Commercial Code (Código Comercial de Macau), approved by Decree-Law No. 40/99/M, as amended, in particular Articles 441 to 474 (Sociedade em Comandita / limited partnership formation, rights and obligations) and Articles 4 to 57 on commercial registration; read together with Administrative Regulation No. 19/2009 on Commercial Registration and the applicable foreign investment rules of the Macao SAR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial and Movable Property Registry (Conservatória do Registo Comercial e de Bens Móveis), Legal Affairs Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Assuntos de Justiça), Macao Special Administrative Region Government
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Macao Commercial Registry Incorporation Application and Notarized Partnership Deed (Requerimento de Registo Comercial e Escritura de Constituição de Sociedade)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital rule applies to this Foreign-Invested Partnership. The partners freely fix the subscribed capital in the Partnership Deed; capital may be contributed in cash, in-kind maritime assets, or qualifying industrial services by general partners. No escrow or blocked-account requirement exists at the commercial registry stage, but the DSEDT Industrial Licensing Division may require a bank guarantee or escrow arrangement for site restoration, waste disposal, and civil defense liabilities before the shipyard obtains final operating approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1/2025 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS / MANAGING GENERAL PARTNERS OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (ISIC 3011 SHIPYARD).

The undersigned directors and general partners, constituting the full governance body of the Partnership, adopt this written resolution on [date] at [time] at the adopted registered office of the Partnership.

WHEREAS: (A) The Partnership is being incorporated as a commercially registered limited partnership in the Macao Special Administrative Region under Articles 441 to 474 of the Macao Commercial Code; (B) the commercial object includes the design, construction, repair, conversion and maintenance of deep-sea dry cargo and container ocean vessels, and the operation of a shipyard and related industrial facilities; (C) the Partnership requires a formal governance record for incorporation, bank account activation, registered-office adoption, statutory officer appointments and industrial licensing applications; (D) the partners intend to fund the Partnership through cash contributions and in-kind maritime equipment contributions.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Incorporation Deed and Registration. The authorized representatives are directed to execute, notarize and submit the Partnership Deed, together with the application for commercial registration, to the Commercial and Movable Property Registry, to pay all statutory fees, to answer official queries, and to obtain the definitive registration certificate.

2. Subscription and Payment of Capital. The subscribed capital set out in the capital schedule of the Partnership Deed is hereby approved. Each general partner and limited partner shall pay or contribute the amount subscribed in accordance with the schedule. No contribution may be returned except upon a legally admitted capital reduction or dissolution.

3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Partnership is adopted at [address, Macao SAR]. The Manager may change the registered office only after the appropriate governmental filing and formal update of official records.

4. Banking and Payment Rails. The following banks are hereby approved: [banks]. The Manager and the jointly-appointed designated signatories are authorized to open operating, escrow and maritime trade accounts in the name of the Partnership, to accept marine installment letters of credit, to execute bank mandates, to borrow within approved limits, to endorse checks and to instruct payments relating to shipyard operations.

5. Statutory Officers. [Name] is appointed Manager and principal statutory officer; [Name] is appointed AML/CFT Compliance Officer; [Name] is appointed Secretary to maintain registers and minutes; [Name] is appointed Safety Manager for site operations. Each officer is empowered to file declarations, represent the Partnership before government bodies and coordinate external legal counsel.

6. Certification. Certified copies of this resolution shall be furnished to the Commercial Registry, DSEDT, DSPA, Fire Services Bureau, Marine and Water Affairs Bureau, banks and insurers.

7. Effectiveness. This resolution takes effect immediately and remains in full force unless and until revoked by a later resolution or required by law.

Adopted and signed on the date first stated above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership Name Reservation and Registry Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial and Movable Property Registry (CRCBM), Legal Affairs Bureau, with coordination through the Macao Trade and Investment Promotion Institute (IPIM) one-stop service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the name-reservation application in Portuguese or Chinese using the official CRCBM form, accompanied by legalized identification documents of all proposed general and limited partners and a power of attorney to a Macao lawyer. The Registry will check identical or confusingly similar names, trademark registers, and prohibited civil or public names. After approval, the approved name is reserved for a 90-day period. If the name is refused, the applicant may submit a new name or file a written objection to the same Registry. The pre-clearance work stream must be coordinated with the designated law firm so that the final deed text can use the approved name without later amendment.
required_dossiers: CRCBM name-reservation application form
Identity documents / passports of all general and limited partners
Notarized power of attorney to the Macao lawyer
Certificate of capacity and board resolution for any corporate partner
Statement of desired business object and ISIC 3011 shipyard scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused or suspended, submit a written objection to CRCBM within 30 days or immediately select an alternative name; if the review exceeds five working days, escalate through IPIM for expedited administrative handling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Macao Notary Public / Licensed Lawyer with notarial powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon name approval, the notary will draft and review the Partnership Deed, including capital schedule, profit-sharing ratio, management powers, audit rights, liquidation events and dispute-resolution clauses. All general and limited partners must appear personally or by valid power of attorney before the Macao notary; foreign corporate partners must produce constitutional documents and a board resolution authorizing the partnership subscription. The notary confirms identity, capacity and independent legal advice, then reads, explains and signs the deed in one public ceremony. Notarized copies are issued for subsequent registration. Any amendment to the deed after execution will require a supplementary notarized act and re-registration.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation certificate
Draft Partnership Deed
Passports or corporate constitutional documents of all partners
Power of attorney for represented partners
Proof of address of each partner
Evidence of in-kind capital contribution, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or delays execution due to legal defects, correct the flagged clauses and re-submit the amended deed; unresolved disputes may be submitted to the Macao Legal Affairs Bureau for an official interpretation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration, Tax Registration and Social Security Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial and Movable Property Registry; Macao Finance Services Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças); Macao Social Security Fund (FSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the authorized lawyer submits the original notarized deed, completed commercial registry application, name certificate, and supporting declarations to the CRCBM for final registration, together with the fee receipt. The CRCBM registers the partnership and issues the definitive commercial registration certificate. In parallel, the Macao Finance Services Bureau and the Social Security Fund are notified through the one-stop procedure to issue the taxpayer registration number and employer registration number. The lawyer must verify that all filed statements match the deed exactly. If the Registry requests amendments, the lawyer responds within the stated period and re-submits without unnecessary delay.
required_dossiers: Notarized Partnership Deed
Approved name reservation certificate
Commercial registration application form
Identities and tax identification numbers of partners
Registered-office consent letter from the property owner
Receipt of payment of registration fees
AML/CFT internal policies and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspension or query, respond with clarifications within 15 working days; if a filing is rejected, rectify the stated non-compliance and pay any re-filing fee; administrative review is available under the Macao Administrative Procedure Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Macao Economic and Technological Development Bureau (DSEDT), Department of Industrial and Technical Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to DSEDT a full industrial license application for the shipyard facility. The dossier must describe dry-dock dimensions, building berths, fabrication shops, coating and blasting areas, water-side infrastructure, cranes, power supply, emergency response and waste collection points. The application must include the commercial registration certificate, registered-office certificate, site lease or ownership certificate, layout drawings, project technical reports, preliminary fire safety documents, pollution prevention plan and evidence that a qualified site safety manager has been appointed. DSEDT will schedule a site inspection, check the installed equipment against the declared processes, and issue the industrial license subject to operational conditions that the Partnership must observe at all times.
required_dossiers: DSEDT industrial establishment application form
Commercial registration certificate
Lease or ownership title to shipyard site
Shipyard layout drawings and equipment list
Process description covering ISIC 3011 activities
Preliminary civil defense fire safety approval
Pollution prevention and waste management plan
Certificate of appointment of safety manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or subject to a negative preliminary inspection, deliver the outstanding technical reports within 10 working days and request a re-inspection; denial may be appealed to the DSEDT Secretary within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment and Civil Defense / Fire Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Macao Environmental Protection Bureau (DSPA); Macao Fire Services Bureau (Corpo de Bombeiros); Lands, Public Works and Transport Bureau (DSSOPT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The environmental consultant will screen the shipyard project under the Macao EIA classification rules. For a Class B project, an EIA report must be prepared addressing dredging, wastewater, air emissions, noise, hazardous waste and marine sediment management, and submitted to DSPA for technical approval. In parallel, the application for civil defense fire safety certification must be lodged with the Fire Services Bureau, accompanied by architectural plans, fire protection system specifications, hazardous material storage licences, evacuation plans and a structural load certificate for dry-dock gates and workshop mezzanines. The agencies may impose operational mitigation measures, monitoring obligations and annual reporting duties that shall become annexed to the industrial license.
required_dossiers: EIA registration form and applicable EIA report
Site survey and marine baseline data
Wastewater and VOC emission management plan
Hazardous waste manifest and disposal contract
Fire protection layout and extinguishing system drawings
Structural load certificates
Evacuation and emergency response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DSPA requires a higher EIA tier or additional studies, commission the supplementary analysis and resubmit within 30 days; if the Fire Services Bureau withholds certification, correct all flagged deficiencies with the fire safety officer and request a fresh inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Marine and Water Affairs Bureau Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed banks in Macao SAR; Macao Marine and Water Affairs Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Assuntos Marítimos e de Água)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration and industrial licensing, execute the banking authorization by presenting the certified resolution and commercial registration certificate to the chosen financial institution, and open operating, tax, escrow and maritime trade accounts. The bank will conduct enhanced due diligence on the general partners and ultimate beneficial owners, and will set up maritime installment letters of credit and escrow payment rails if requested. Concurrently, apply to the Macao Marine and Water Affairs Bureau for the shipyard site operating permit, berth and dry-dock use authorization, navigational signalling approval and waste-disposal interface approval. Only after receipt of all clearances may the shipyard commence commercial production.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the First Board Resolution
Commercial registration certificate and partnership deed
Tax registration number
DSEDT industrial license
DSPA environmental approval
Fire Services Bureau certificate
Shipyard site lease or title
Marine insurance and P&I insurance certificates
Beneficial ownership declaration for bank due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide the updated registry extract and contractual documentation; if the Marine and Water Affairs Bureau delays, request an expedited inter-bureau review through IPIM.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Macao Economic and Technological Development Bureau (DSEDT), Industrial Licensing Division; Macao Trade and Investment Promotion Institute (IPIM) for investor facilitation; Macao Marine and Water Affairs Bureau for port-adjacent yard operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial License for Shipbuilding and Ship Repair (Licença Industrial para Construção e Reparação Naval), supplemented by the Shipyard Site Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Macao Environmental Protection Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Protecção Ambiental, DSPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Registration and Preliminary EIA Report required; a Full EIA Report may be required if the shipyard area exceeds five hectares or the site lies within a water protection zone. A marine environmental study and an Environmental Registration Certificate are mandatory for dry-dock operations adjacent to Macao waters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges from blasting, painting, cooling and yard runoff must comply with pH 6-9, suspended solids ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 150 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 60 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L, copper ≤ 0.5 mg/L and zinc ≤ 2 mg/L. VOC abatement systems must achieve at least 80% destruction efficiency, with solvent loading not exceeding 0.1 kg per square metre of coated surface. Hazardous waste, including spent antifouling paint, blast debris and used oils, must be stored in sealed containers for not more than 180 days and transported by a licensed waste carrier under a fully documented manifest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Macao Fire Services Bureau (Corpo de Bombeiros), confirming compliance with fire-resistance ratings, emergency exits, active fire suppression, flammable-liquid storage limits and on-site emergency response. The structural clearance for dry-dock structures, workshops, cranes and piers must be issued by the Lands, Public Works and Transport Bureau (DSSOPT), together with a workplace safety clearance from the Labour Affairs Bureau (DSAL) covering occupational safety, personal protective equipment, confined-space entry, hot work and noise exposure limits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Finance Services Bureau of the Macao Special Administrative Region (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças, DSF), official online tax services portal: https://www.dsf.gov.mo
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested partnership (FIP) intending to operate a commercial shipyard in Macao, the following procedure applies. Step 1: Execute the partnership deed in accordance with the Macao Commercial Code and obtain any required foreign-investment approval from the Macao Trade and Investment Promotion Institute (IPIM), if the activity triggers sectoral FDI screening. Step 2: Register the partnership at the Commercial and Movable Property Registry (Registo Comercial e de Bens Móveis) and obtain the Commercial Registration number. Step 3: Submit the statutory Commencement of Business Declaration (Declaração de Início de Actividade) to the DSF, identifying the partnership's registered address, partners, registered scope limited to shipbuilding, and the effective commencement date. Step 4: The DSF will inscribe the FIP in the taxpayer registry and issue the Macao Taxpayer Number (Número de Contribuinte), which is the sole TIN-equivalent used for all tax filings, customs declarations, and commercial invoicing. Step 5: If the partnership is a foreign non-resident partnership with no place of effective management in Macao, the non-resident partners must appoint a fiscal representative domiciled in Macao to receive tax notifications and service of process from the DSF. Step 6: The FIP must keep the DSF registration current, filing any amendment to partners, registered capital, or business location within the applicable legal time limits. A mainland China TIN or foreign partnership tax identification cannot substitute for the Macao Taxpayer Number when filing Macao tax returns or export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Macao does not administer a check-the-box election, a functional-currency election, or any OECD-style hybrid-mismatch election. The FIP is automatically treated as fiscally transparent for Complementary Income Tax (Imposto Complementar de Rendimentos) purposes, with profits and losses allocated to partners in proportion to their partnership interests and taxed at partner level. Hybrid mismatch rules have not been enacted in Macao.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Selective Consumption Tax (Imposto de Consumo) - a goods excise/sales tax; Macao does not impose any general VAT or GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable in Macanese Pataca (MOP). There is no turnover-based VAT or GST registration threshold in Macao. Consumption Tax obligations, if any, arise only upon importation or local manufacture of goods specified in the Macao Consumption Tax tariff. A shipyard exporting newly built deep-sea dry cargo and container vessels is not required to register for Consumption Tax solely by reason of turnover, and vessel exports are not subject to Consumption Tax because the goods are not consumed in Macao.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable. Macao operates no real-time fiscal clearance system, no tax-authority e-invoicing API, and no anti-fraud digital stamping or mandatory electronic clearance obligation. Commercial invoices and accounting records must be issued and retained in accordance with the Macao Commercial Code and DSF bookkeeping and audit requirements, and are subject to inspection during tax audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Macao does not have a VAT zero-rating mechanism because it does not levy VAT or GST on exports. For Consumption Tax purposes, an ocean container vessel sold to a foreign shipowner and physically exported from Macao is outside the indirect tax net. The shipyard must substantiate that the vessel left Macao customs territory and that no domestic consumption, charter-in, installation, or use in Macao occurred. The export treatment is documented through the Macao Customs Service export procedure rather than through a VAT zero-rating certificate. No input VAT refund is available because there is no VAT input-credit system in Macao.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaração de Exportação) accepted by the Macao Customs Service (Serviços de Alfândega de Macau)
Original commercial invoice and sale contract for the deep-sea container vessel
Bill of Lading or sea waybill evidencing shipment from Macao to the foreign buyer
Freight and insurance documents reflecting the agreed Incoterm, such as FOB or CIF
Bank settlement and foreign-exchange receipt evidence, such as letter-of-credit negotiation advice or telegraphic-transfer credit advice from a Macao bank
Vessel delivery protocol and sea-trial completion certificate, if required by customs, confirming delivery to the foreign purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or unsubstantiated export documentation can cause the DSF and Macao Customs Service to disregard the export treatment, reassess the partnership, deny the exclusion from Consumption Tax, and impose additional Complementary Income Tax, default interest, and fines under the Macao tax offence regime (Regime Juridico das Infracções Tributarias). Fraudulent or knowingly incorrect declarations may be treated as tax fraud and prosecuted under the Macao Penal Code with penalties including monetary fines and imprisonment. Because Macao does not operate a VAT input-credit system, there is no VAT input-refund clawback; however, any customs duty exemption or export-related tax benefit can be retrospectively clawed back and reassessed within the applicable legal limitation period if the underlying export documents are found to be false or misleading.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Monetary Authority of Macao (Autoridade Monetária de Macau, AMCM)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Macao SAR operates an open, low-restriction monetary regime supervised by AMCM rather than a traditional central bank. The Macanese pataca (MOP) is freely convertible within the territory and remains stable through a managed peg to the Hong Kong dollar (HKD). Current account transactions, including export revenue, shipping freight, and vessel-related charges, are fully liberalised and do not require case-by-case foreign exchange approval. Capital account items, such as equity injection from non-resident partners, loan repayment, and dividend distribution, are also unrestricted under Macao law; however, movements of RMB from mainland China remain subject to the mainland's State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registration and cross-border RMB schemes. No export surrender rules apply in Macao, and no minimum conversion ratio exists for shipyard export proceeds. Profit repatriation from a Foreign-Invested Partnership is evidence-based rather than approval-based: the partner must present audited financial statements, the partnership distribution resolution, and proof of Macao tax settlement, after which funds can be remitted freely via licensed banks. The principal compliance friction is documentary, not regulatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists in Macao SAR. Exporters may retain, freely convert, or deploy foreign currency receipts according to commercial needs. For RMB receipts from mainland counterparties, the shipyard must maintain the underlying trade contract and customs declaration, and settlement must pass through AMCM-licensed banks using CIPS or correspondent clearing; there is no mandated conversion into MOP or HKD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with multi-currency MOP/HKD/USD capability and trade services
Capital Escrow Account and Maritime Installment Letter of Credit Services Account
Multi-Currency Corporate Current Account and Escrow Sub-Account for construction milestone payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI and virtual-bank style platforms have negligible viability for servicing a Macao-domiciled shipyard company. AMCM has not granted a banking or payment-institution licence to any branchless EMI targeting local entities, and the Macao Financial System Act and AMCM payment guidelines effectively reserve deposit-taking and account operation for licensed credit institutions with a physical presence in Macao. Such fintechs cannot open MOP settlement accounts, issue SWIFT identifiers, or handle trade documentary operations for the shipyard. Consequently, cross-border treasury must rely on traditional AMCM-licensed banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one statutory partner and one authorised signatory must appear physically in-branch for the original KYC interview; remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted by Macao banks for foreign-invested partnerships. After the face-to-face meeting, a local manager may be appointed as a secondary authorised signatory under a notarised power of attorney, but the partner identity remains ultimately accountable to AMCM-required beneficial owner due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex and opaque beneficial ownership engineered through a pass-through partnership structure with multiple shell partners in low-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A structural diagram showing every legal entity up the chain to each natural person holding 25% or more, certified partnership deed, certified registry extracts from each partner's jurisdiction, shareholder registers, and sworn declarations acknowledging ultimate beneficial ownership of the shipyard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The commercial shipbuilding activity involves high-value milestone payments and large advance payments that may appear inconsistent with ordinary cost bases, raising trade-based money laundering valuation flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed shipyard contract with liquidated damages and payment schedule, independent marine engineer's cost build-up appraisal, third-party hull valuation, insurance schedules for the vessel under construction, and audited shipyard financial statements for the last two fiscal years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of a non-resident Chinese partner connected to state-owned entities or holding a politically exposed person status, creating enhanced-scrutiny sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level PEP and sanctions screening report from a commercial screening database such as Dow Jones or Refinitiv, government-issued proof of source of funds, fund movement history for 12 months, and an independent legal opinion explaining the absence of corruption or misappropriation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential naval or dual-use application of vessels, with allegations of deliveries to embargoed operators or routes requiring special military-end-use screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IMO ship number and classification society certificate confirming commercial dry cargo/container vessel design, final end-user certificate from the charterer or buyer, denial orders database check from the Statutory Trade Control authorities, and an export classification memo from a licensed maritime law firm confirming absence of military application.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident partners should route capital contributions via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the shipyard's AMCM-licensed bank account, clearly using payment narrative 'Foreign-Invested Partnership Equity Injection' and referencing the entity registration number. For inward remittances from mainland China in RMB, the sender must apply the SAFE foreign investment registration code and use CIPS-compatible channels; the Macao receiving bank will perform an economic substance check before crediting the capital escrow account. Upon credit, a certified Macao CPA or external auditor must issue a capital contribution confirmation report registering the capital increase in the commercial registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The shipyard should use SWIFT MT103 high-value clearing for supplier invoices, subcontractor payroll and domestic operating expenses, while major imported steel plate and ship equipment purchases should be settled through irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) with payment deferred against presentation of clean documents. Documentary Collections may be used for recurring low-risk marine consumables. Vessel deliveries may receive payment under a Maritime Installment L/C or via an escrow account against electronic bill of lading and commercial invoice. All outward RMB payments must retain underlying contracts and customs declarations to withstand mainland SAFE audits when counterparties are in China.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot and vanilla outright forward contracts in MOP/HKD/USD up to one-year tenor, supported by the underlying shipbuilding contract and matched to scheduled milestone receipts or steel procurement payments.
Cross-currency basis swaps between MOP, HKD, and USD used strictly to align currency mismatches between funded capital, construction costs, and contractual sale price.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked through AMCM-licensed banks to hedge RMB-denominated costs or revenues from mainland Chinese subcontractors; onshore CNY NDFs are not permissible within Macao.
Currency options are not permitted unless expressly approved by the AMCM in writing, and speculative trading outside the enterprise's trade exposure is rejected in entity-level treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Macao Commercial Code (Código Comercial) for a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Commercial Registry (Registo Comercial) / Macao Legal and Registration Bureau (DSRJ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of the anniversary of the entity's registration date; extensions are not granted for annual return filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of MOP 300 (approx. USD 37) for the first month; further delay may result in suspension of the commercial registration certificate and, after 60 days of continued non-filing, initiation of administrative dissolution or strike-off proceedings by the Macao Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of the Registered Office Address and Managing Partners/Management Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Commercial Registry (Registo Comercial) and local tax authority (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças - DSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 September for changes effectuated by 31 August; otherwise the standard 15-day post-event notification rule applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation triggers a MOP 1,000 (approx. USD 125) administrative fine; persistent default beyond the calendar year end is registered as an irregularity and may preclude issuance of official certificates; further delay can lead to registration suspension and a strike-off docket.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of taxable income and business activity (declaração anual de rendimentos) for the pass-through partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Financial Services Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças - DSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 April and 30 June of the following tax year; extensions are not permitted for the base annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from MOP 1,000 to MOP 10,000 (approx. USD 125 to 1,250) depending on the magnitude of taxable income omitted; criminal tax default penalties may apply for fraudulent omissions; after the administrative collection phase, the entity may be declared administratively inactive and subject to forced strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual occupational tax renewal (Contribuição Industrial/Industrial Tax) for the shipyard manufacturing activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Financial Services Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Finanças - DSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: In February and March of each year, with the final payment date on 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-payment surcharge of 5% per month up to a maximum of 30% of the assessed tax; failure to renew the industrial registration by 31 May may result in partial or complete suspension of the industrial license and the authority to operate the shipyard; extended non-compliance leads to administrative strike-off of the industrial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the maritime/shipyard operating license and environmental registration certificate (Companhia de Construção Naval / Estaleiro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Maritime and Water Bureau (Direcção dos Serviços de Assuntos Marítimos e de Água - DSAMA); also environmental licensing desk under DSF if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 December of each calendar year for the following year; license renewal applications must be submitted no earlier than 30 November
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal by 31 January results in automatic suspension of shipbuilding operations and a fine of MOP 5,000 (approx. USD 625); continued operation without a valid license is an administrative breach carrying additional daily fines of MOP 200 (approx. USD 25); after 180 days of suspension, the license is revoked and the partnership is listed for strike-off in the regulatory registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Charges and Mortgages - annual update filing (including maritime vessel mortgages and ship construction hypothecation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Commercial Registry (Registo Comercial) and Macao Maritime Registry (Registo Marítimo of DSAMA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the date of any charge creation, variation, or discharge; in the absence of charge events, an annual nil confirmation is required by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The charge is unenforceable against third parties until registered; failure to file the annual nil confirmation results in a MOP 500 (approx. USD 62) fine and suspension of certified copies; persistent non-filing after three months permits compulsory rectification at the partnership's expense and strike-off consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration and payment of crew/social security fund contributions (only if shipyard has maritime construction crew payroll)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Macao Social Security Fund (Fundo de Segurança Social - FSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly contributions due on the last business day of the following month; annual declaration of all registered employees due by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at the annual statutory rate of 10%; administrative fines may reach MOP 5,000 (approx. USD 625) per employee for knowingly under-declared payroll; continued non-payment is certified by the FSS to the Commercial Registry and may result in the blocking of annual commercial registrations and eventual dissolution order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is compulsory where: (a) the annual turnover of the partnership exceeds MOP 5 million (approx. USD 620,000); (b) the total balance sheet assets exceed MOP 3 million (approx. USD 372,000); (c) the partnership has more than 50 employees during the fiscal year; (d) the entity is a foreign-invested partnership with foreign corporate or non-resident partners that have contributed in excess of MOP 2 million (approx. USD 248,000); or (e) the partnership operates a licensed shipyard under the jurisdiction of the Macao Maritime and Water Bureau, because the maritime sector is considered an activity of public interest. For entities that fall below these thresholds, a voluntary audit is permitted under the Macao Companies Act and Auditing Standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Where an audit is required, the applicable framework is Macao Financial Reporting Standards which are aligned with IFRS for large partnerships; small- and medium-sized partnerships may use the Macao SME Financial Reporting Framework which is materially convergent with the IFRS for SMEs; all exempted entities must nonetheless prepare annual accounts under the minimum statutory principles of the Macao Commercial Code (Código Comercial).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Macao has implemented statutory beneficial ownership transparency measures requiring every legal person, including foreign-invested partnerships, to maintain an accurate internal register of ultimate beneficial owners. An annual confirmation of the UBO register must be submitted to the Macao Commercial Registry within 30 days after the anniversary of registration, certifying that the beneficial ownership information in the internal register is complete and accurate. On any shareholding or partnership interest transfer resulting in a change of beneficial ownership, the partnership is legally required to update the internal UBO register within 30 days of the change and file a change notice with the Commercial Registry within 60 days of the transfer. If a beneficial owner holds an interest through a chain of entities, the Macao authority accepts a written declaration identifying the natural person who ultimately exercises control; however, the entity must be prepared to disclose the full ownership chain on official request. Sanctions for non-compliance with UBO disclosures include fines up to MOP 20,000 (approx. USD 2,480) per violation and corporate registration sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 to USD 8,500 per audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12% maximum marginal rate of Macao SAR Complementary Income Tax (Imposto Complementar de Rendimentos); first MOP 600,000 of assessable profits exempt
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For ISIC 3011 shipbuilding FIP, no general free-zone patent-box rate is available; the annual tax benefits package exempts the first MOP 600,000 of taxable profit, and qualifying R&D vessel design costs may benefit from an extra deduction under Macao's technology incentive scheme; offshore-regime tax holidays do not apply because the shipyard's core income-generating activities are onshore in Macao

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo M/1 (Declaracao Anual do Imposto Complementar de Rendimentos) filed via the DSF e-Financas portal of the Direccao dos Servicos de Financas; audited financial statements and tax reconciliation schedules attached as annexes
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year Macao FIP, the M/1 return must be filed no later than 30 June following the fiscal year-end; a two-month extension may be requested before the normal deadline; the DSF may also direct a special filing date in the notice of assessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the taxpayer: full legal name, TIN/NIF number, registered address, legal form (FIP), and date of incorporation in Macao.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Macao NIF of the FIP. A non-resident partner or mainland China parent must be identified separately with its China tax identification number and address. If the FIP has no physical Macao office for the shipyard, this is the first red flag that the DSF will examine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period and tax status: calendar year end and status as Group A or Group B taxpayer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A FIP with imported capital and intercompany shipbuilding contracts is normally Group A and must attach audited accounts. If the centre of effective management is claimed in Macao, evidence must include board minutes and management decisions signed in Macao.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue: proceeds from construction and sale of ocean container vessels, progress billings, price escalation clauses and related shipyard income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Macao-source revenue should be included. Export sales to the mainland parent must be at arm's length; advances received under maritime LC and escrow accounts are not recognized until performance obligations are satisfied if accrual accounting applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct ship construction expenditures: steel hull procurement, marine engines, dry-dock services, labour and subcontracting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident related-party purchases, use the import-customs declaration and transfer pricing file. Undocumented labour subcontractor invoices are automatically disallowed; benchmarked CUP or TNMM evidence must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: administrative, rents, utilities, insurance, professional fees, depreciation of shipyard assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a mainland parent charges management fees or know-how royalties, the deduction is capped at the arm's length amount and requires actual provision plus documentation; otherwise the FIP must add back in Box 7.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating and financial items: interest income, exchange adjustments, government subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest from intercompany loans should be reported at the contractual rate, with a maximum 7% treaty cap for non-resident lenders under the China-Macau Arrangement; late-payment interest to a foreign affiliate is not deductible if it is not fully supported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation: add-back of non-deductible expenses and adjustments from audited profit to assessable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any transfer pricing adjustment proposed by the DSF; non-resident partner drawings are not deductible and must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward and statutory tax exemption: enter prior losses within the five-year carryforward window and the MOP 600,000 exempt amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same loss cannot be used in the Macao FIP and the mainland China parent; only Macao statutory losses and the yearly legislative exemption amount are allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complementary tax computation: apply the progressive bands and 12% maximum rate on the remaining assessable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Macao pataca (MOP) only; if accounts are kept in RMB, translate at the DSF official exchange rate and attach the rate certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and treaty relief: foreign tax credits and China-Macau Arrangement application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the mainland parent is the beneficial owner of dividend, interest or royalty payments, complete the treaty schedule and attach the Macao Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement; without these, the 5% dividend or 7% cap is unavailable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of M/1 triggers a DSF fine of MOP 1,000 to MOP 10,000, plus a 5% monthly surcharge for each commenced month up to a maximum of 15%; if tax is understated, the difference attracts a 100% surcharge and default interest at the DSF current rate; if fraudulent declarations are made, criminal tax evasion thresholds under Macau Penal Code Articles 250 and 251 apply with imprisonment up to 8 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Macao does not impose withholding tax on dividend distributions by an FIP; however, under the China-Macau Arrangement, where a mainland China corporate partner holds at least 25%, the treaty rate is 5%; otherwise 10%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For payment streams that are not already exempt, the investor must (1) obtain a Macao Tax Residency Certificate from the DSF; (2) obtain a China Tax Residency Certificate from the State Taxation Administration; (3) submit the DSF treaty-relief annex before the payment; (4) provide a beneficial ownership declaration stating the partner has no intermediate conduit and has full economic ownership of the proceeds; (5) keep certification for at least 5 years for inspection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding is 0%, but if loan interest is profit-participating or paid to a non-resident related enterprise without a banking intermediary, it may be recharacterized as a deemed distribution and exempt; royalties for patents, know-how, copyright and industrial designs paid to a non-resident are subject to a final withholding of 5%; under the China-Macau Arrangement, interest and royalties are capped at 7%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Macao has no enacted Local File threshold in the DSF regulations; under BEPS Action 13 administrative practice, a Local File must be prepared if aggregate controlled transactions exceed MOP 5,000,000 in a fiscal year, and a Master File is recommended if the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Macao offshore substance doctrine and OECD Forum on Harmful Tax Practices require that an FIP's core income-generating activities (CIGA) for shipyard operations—steel procurement, construction supervision, dry-dock scheduling, risk-bearing and final invoicing—be performed in Macao with fit-for-purpose staffing and premises. If CIGA are conducted by the mainland parent in Guangzhou or Shanghai, the DSF may deny treaty benefits, annul the license, and re-assess income in the hands of the Macao FIP; a shell FIP without substance has no entitlement to China-Macau Arrangement relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP understates the sale price of ocean container vessels, fabricates subcontractor invoices for dry-dock work, or records non-existent steel purchases to reduce assessable profit below the MOP 600,000 exemption threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DSF issues an additional assessment of the hidden profit plus 100% surcharge; an administrative fine of MOP 20,000 to MOP 500,000 is imposed; criminal proceedings may be initiated under Macau Penal Code Article 250 (tax fraud) and Article 251 (aggravated fraud), with imprisonment up to 8 years and daily fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Macau courts may pierce the FIP's veil under Civil Code Article 227 for abuse of legal personality. Directors are personally liable for the unpaid tax and surcharges; the DSF can impose a travel ban and blacklist (impedimento de saida) where tax debt exceeds MOP 10,000; in egregious maritime procurement fraud, directors face criminal imprisonment of two to eight years and restitution of contractors' funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The mainland China parent supplies hull blocks and marine engines to the Macao FIP at inflated prices, or the Macao FIP invoices vessel sales at a marked-down price without a written service or contract agreement, shifting profits to a lower-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DSF performs an arm's length adjustment under OECD principles and Article 45 of the Complementary Tax Code; the understated profit is taxed at up to 12%, plus a 5% monthly late-payment surcharge, and a coercive fine of up to MOP 200,000 for non-production of the transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false intercompany contracts are jointly liable for the tax adjustment; civil liability for malpractice is triggered; the Commercial Register may suspend the FIP's license; if the profit shifting is supported by false invoices, criminal forgery charges and imprisonment of up to 5 years apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, economic substance failure and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Macao FIP is only a paper entity: no Macao employees, no local board decision-making, no shipyard premises, while all core income-generating activities are performed at the mainland shipbuilding group; the FIP continues to claim China-Macau Arrangement benefits on dividends, interest and royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DSF and the Macao Finance Bureau deny DTA benefits, revoke the FIP's Macao registration or license, and recover taxes for the prior six years; fines under the Macao offshore regime may reach MOP 500,000; the entity is treated under anti-abuse rules as fiscally transparent for the mainland parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee directors can be declared jointly liable for all recovered taxes; personal travel bans and blacklisting by the DSF are typical; if the shell structure is used for money laundering connected to maritime payments, directors are prosecuted under Macao AML Law with imprisonment of up to 8 years, asset forfeiture, and restitution.
